definitions.explanation: The number seven. Like four, seven has two readings: なな and しち. なな is more commonly used in everyday counting because しち can be confused with いち (one) or し (four) when spoken.

examples.japanese: {七|なな}{時|じ}に{会|あ}いましょう。
{一|いっ}{週間|しゅうかん}は{七|なな}{日|にち}です。
{七|なな}{月|がつ}に{日本|にほん}へ{行|い}きます。
examples.english: I'm going to Japan in July.
examples.notes: しちがつ is also correct

examples.japanese: {七|なな}つの{山|やま}を{見|み}ました。とても{大|おお}きかったです。
examples.english: I saw seven mountains. They were very big.

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}は{七|なな}{人|にん}{家族|かぞく}です。{父|ちち}と{母|はは}と{兄弟|きょうだい}がいます。
examples.english: My family has seven people. I have a father, mother, and siblings.

notes: Both なな and しち are correct readings, but なな is preferred in most spoken contexts for clarity. しち is used in {七|しち}{月|がつ} (July) and sometimes {七|しち}{時|じ} (seven o'clock), though なながつ and ななじ are increasingly common. The native counter is {七|なな}つ (nanatsu).
